question: What is the value of the radius of the earth? (RRB Technician Grade III (23/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: 5400 km
6400 km
7400 km
8400 km
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6400 km

Explanation:
The radius of the Earth is approximately 6400 kilometers (or 6371 km). This is a fundamental fact in geography and astronomy. Earth is not a perfect sphere; it is slightly flattened at the poles, so its average radius is taken as 6371 km. The equatorial radius is about 6378 km, and the polar radius is about 6357 km. In competitive exams, the approximate value of 6400 km is often asked.

☛ Equatorial radius → 6378 km
☛ Polar radius → 6357 km
☛ Circumference of Earth → about 40,000 km
☛ Mass of Earth → about 5.972 × 10^24 kg

question: Which of the following forces is responsible for the tides, due to the Moon and the Sun? (RRB Technician Grade III (24/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Nuclear force
Electromagnetic force
Electrostatic force
Gravitation force
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gravitation force

Explanation:
Tides are primarily caused by the gravitational force of the Moon and the Sun. The Moon's gravitational pull on Earth is not uniform; it varies across different parts of the Earth. This differential gravitational force creates a bulge in the ocean water, resulting in tides. Although the Sun also exerts gravitational force, its effect is weaker than the Moon's due to its greater distance. The interaction of gravitational forces among Earth, Moon, and Sun leads to high and low tides. No other force, such as nuclear, electromagnetic, or electrostatic force, is responsible for tides.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Primary cause of tides → Gravitational force of the Moon
☛ Role of the Sun in tides → Secondary, due to larger distance
☛ High tide occurs when → Moon and Sun are aligned (full moon/new moon)
☛ Low tide occurs when → Moon and Sun are at 90° (neap tide)
☛ Gravitational force formula → F = G M1 M2 / r^2

question: Which of the following statements is/are correct related to the eco-system?(i) Ozone is a molecule formed by three atoms of oxygen.(ii) Oxygen (O2) is essential for all aerobic forms of life.(iii) Ozone is non-poisonous. (RRB Technician Grade III (24/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: (i), (ii) and (iii)
Only (i) and (ii)
Only (i) and (iii)
Only (i)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only (i) and (ii)

Explanation:
In the ecosystem, ozone and oxygen play crucial roles. Statement (i) is correct because ozone (O₃) is a molecule formed by three atoms of oxygen. It is found in the upper atmosphere and absorbs ultraviolet radiation. Statement (ii) is correct because oxygen (O₂) is essential for all aerobic forms of life, used in respiration. Statement (iii) is incorrect because ozone is a poisonous gas. At ground level, it acts as a pollutant causing respiratory problems. Hence only statements (i) and (ii) are correct.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Where is the ozone layer located? → Stratosphere
☛ What is the chemical formula of ozone? → O₃
☛ Which gas damages the ozone layer? → Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
☛ Which gas is required for aerobic respiration? → Oxygen (O₂)
☛ What is the main source of oxygen on Earth? → Photosynthesis
question_hi: पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र से संबंधित निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?(i) ओज़ोन ऑक्सीजन के तीन परमाणुओं से बना एक अणु है।(ii) ऑक्सीजन (O2) जीवन के सभी वायुजीवी रूपों के लिए आवश्यक है।(iii) ओज़ोन विषहीन है। (RRB Technician Grade III (24/12/2024) Shift 3)

केवल (i) और (ii)
केवल (i) और (iii)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र में ओज़ोन और ऑक्सीजन महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं। कथन (i) सही है क्योंकि ओज़ोन (O₃) ऑक्सीजन के तीन परमाणुओं से मिलकर बना एक अणु है। यह ऊपरी वायुमंडल में पाया जाता है और पराबैंगनी विकिरण को अवशोषित करता है। कथन (ii) सही है क्योंकि ऑक्सीजन (O₂) सभी वायुजीवी जीवों के लिए आवश्यक है, जो श्वसन प्रक्रिया में उपयोग होती है। कथन (iii) गलत है क्योंकि ओज़ोन विषैली गैस है। जमीनी स्तर पर यह प्रदूषक बनकर श्वसन संबंधी समस्याएं पैदा कर सकती है। इसलिए केवल कथन (i) और (ii) सही हैं।

question:
Which of the following crops increases the natural fertility of soils through nitrogen
fixation? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Pulses
Oilseeds
Root vegetables
Cereal grains
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pulses

Explanation:
Pulse crops have a symbiotic relationship with Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules, which fix atmospheric nitrogen into the soil. This process, known as biological nitrogen fixation, naturally enhances soil fertility. Leguminous plants like pulses, grams, and peas are well-known for this ability. In contrast, oilseeds, root vegetables, and cereals deplete soil nutrients without fixing nitrogen. Therefore, growing pulses improves soil fertility by increasing nitrogen content.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Bacterium responsible for nitrogen fixation → Rhizobium
☛ Structure on roots of leguminous plants → Root nodules
☛ Examples of pulse crops → Moong, gram, pea
☛ Enzyme involved in nitrogen fixation → Nitrogenase
☛ Nutrient increased in soil after pulse cultivation → Nitrogen

question:
India's first bullet train project is under construction between which of the following
cities? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Mumbai - Bangalore
Chennai - Hyderabad
Delhi - Lucknow
Ahmedabad - Mumbai
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ahmedabad - Mumbai

Explanation:
India's first bullet train project is the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail Corridor, which is under construction between Maharashtra and Gujarat. It is being developed with Japanese collaboration and has a total length of approximately 508 kilometers. The project will have 12 stations, including Mumbai, Surat, Vadodara, and Ahmedabad. The train will run at a maximum speed of 320 km/h, reducing travel time from the current 8 hours to about 3.5 hours. This project is based on Japanese Shinkansen technology and its cost is around ₹1.08 lakh crore.

question: Which of the following states is known for extensive cultivation of coffee in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Karnataka
Punjab
Assam
Maharashtra
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Karnataka

Explanation:
In India, coffee cultivation is mainly done in the hilly regions of South India. Karnataka accounts for about 71% of India's total coffee production, making it the largest producer. The state primarily grows Arabica and Robusta varieties. Districts like Chikmagalur, Kodagu, and Hassan are prominent for coffee due to their suitable climate and altitude. After Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu are the other major producers. Coffee is grown as a plantation crop and requires a shaded environment. The Coffee Board of India is headquartered in Bengaluru.

question: Which of the following are the two main fibre crops grown in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Rayon and Nylon
Cotton and Jute
Flax and Hemp
Wool and Silk
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cotton and Jute

Explanation:
The two main fibre crops grown in India are cotton and jute. Cotton is a major cash crop used for making cotton textiles. Jute, known as the 'golden fibre', is used for making bags, ropes, etc. Rayon and nylon are synthetic fibres; flax and hemp are oilseed/medicinal crops; wool and silk are obtained from animals/silkworms, not crops. In India, Gujarat is the leading producer of cotton, while West Bengal is the largest producer of jute.

question: During the winter months, the weather conditions in India are primarily influenced by the high-pressure system over which region? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Central and Southern Europe
Central and Western Australia
Central and Eastern Asia
Central and Western Asia
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Central and Western Asia

Explanation:
During the winter months (December to February), weather conditions in India are primarily influenced by a high-pressure system located over Central and Western Asia. This region, particularly near Iran, Turkey, and the Arabian Peninsula, develops a anticyclone that pushes cold, dry north-easterly winds towards India. These winds are known as the Northeast Monsoon or Winter Monsoon, bringing clear skies and cool weather to most parts of India. Only the southeastern coastal areas (e.g., Tamil Nadu) receive rainfall during this season as these winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal. Thus, the high-pressure area over Western Asia is the key factor shaping India's winter climate.

question: Which of the following vegetation types are common in the Thar desert? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Dense temperate forests
Tropical evergreen forests
Xerophytic shrubs and grasses
Mangroves
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Xerophytic shrubs and grasses

Explanation:
The Thar desert is a hot and arid region with annual rainfall less than 25 cm. The vegetation found here is mainly xerophytic (drought-tolerant) type, consisting of thorny shrubs, grasses, and small trees. This vegetation is adapted to survive with little water, such as having thick leaves or deep roots. Dense temperate forests require moisture, tropical evergreen forests occur in high rainfall areas, and mangroves grow in coastal swamps. Therefore, only drought-tolerant shrubs and grasses are common in the Thar desert.

question: The frequency and paths of the tropical depressions originating from the Bay of Bengal are mainly determined by the position of which of the following? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
Equator
Tropic of Capricorn
Tropic of Cancer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)

Explanation:
The frequency and paths of tropical depressions originating from the Bay of Bengal are mainly determined by the position of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). The ITCZ is a low-pressure belt where trade winds from both hemispheres converge, leading to enhanced convective activity and cyclone formation. Its seasonal migration influences the frequency and track of cyclones in the Bay of Bengal. The Equator, Tropic of Capricorn, and Tropic of Cancer are fixed latitudinal lines, while the ITCZ is dynamic.

question: Which of the following is a zero waste procedure? (RRB JE CBT 2 (Electronics Engineering) ReExam (04/06/2025))
options: Pest management
Organic farming
Integrated organic farming
Inorganic farming
solution:

Explanation:

This system eliminates waste by using by-products as inputs, such as using animal manure as fertilizer and crop residues as animal feed. In contrast, pest management, organic farming, and inorganic farming generate waste. Integrated organic farming is a closed-loop system that reduces environmental impact and maximizes resource efficiency. It integrates various components like crops, livestock, and waste management to achieve sustainability.

question: What are the sand dunes commonly found in the Indian Desert called? (RRB JE CBT 2 (Electronics Engineering) ReExam (04/06/2025))

Moraines
Cirques
solution:

Explanation:
The sand dunes commonly found in the Indian Desert (Thar Desert) are called Barchans. These are crescent-shaped dunes that open their horns (tips) in the direction of the wind. Barchan dunes form in arid regions with constant wind direction and limited sand supply, primarily through wind erosion and deposition. In India, they are mainly found in the Thar Desert of Rajasthan. These landforms are significant in geography as they indicate wind activity. Other options: Loess is fine silt deposited by wind, Moraines are glacial deposits, and Cirques are semicircular basins formed by glacial erosion.

question: The area termed as the ozone hole is known to mainly develop over ______. (RRB JE CBT 2 (Electronics Engineering) ReExam (04/06/2025))
options: India
Africa
Antartica
America
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Antarctica

Explanation:
The ozone hole refers to the thinning or depletion of the ozone layer in the Earth's stratosphere. This phenomenon mainly develops over Antarctica during the southern hemisphere's spring. The ozone hole is caused by the release of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and other harmful chemicals that break down ozone molecules. The extremely cold temperatures in Antarctica create polar stratospheric clouds, which accelerate ozone-depleting reactions. International efforts like the Montreal Protocol (1987) have helped in the recovery of the ozone layer by banning the production of CFCs. Antarctica experiences the most severe ozone depletion compared to other regions. The ozone hole leads to increased ultraviolet (UV) radiation reaching the Earth's surface, which poses health risks like skin cancer.

☛ During which season does the ozone hole typically occur? → Spring

The Western Ghats, Satpura Hills, and Vindhya Hills are located in different parts of India, but only the Aravali Hills lie on the western edge of the Thar Desert. This mountain range is one of the oldest fold mountains in the world, formed during the Precambrian era.

question: Which of the following regions in India is known for the Shola forests? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which factor plays the most dominant role in the seasonal reversal of wind direction in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Ocean currents
Relief
Latitude
Monsoonal pressure system
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Monsoonal pressure system

Explanation:
The seasonal reversal of wind direction in India is primarily caused by the monsoonal pressure system. During summer, the Asian landmass heats up intensely, creating a low-pressure center, while the Indian Ocean remains relatively cooler, forming a high-pressure area. This pressure gradient drives the southwest monsoon winds. In winter, the pattern reverses, leading to northeast monsoon winds. This phenomenon is driven by the uneven heating of land and water. Factors like ocean currents, relief, and latitude also influence the climate, but the monsoonal pressure system plays the most dominant role in seasonal wind reversal.

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है ग्रेट इंडियन बस्टर्ड

Explanation:
डेजर्ट नेशनल पार्क राजस्थान के थार मरुस्थल में स्थित है। यह ग्रेट इंडियन बस्टर्ड (गोडावण) नामक लुप्तप्राय पक्षी के लिए प्रसिद्ध है। यह पक्षी भारत के वन्यजीव संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1972 की अनुसूची I में शामिल है। इसकी संख्या तेजी से घट रही है और इसे IUCN रेड लिस्ट में गंभीर रूप से लुप्तप्राय श्रेणी में रखा गया है। डेजर्ट नेशनल पार्क इसके संरक्षण के लिए महत्वपूर्ण स्थल है। यहाँ रेगिस्तानी लोमड़ी, चिंकारा और सर्प भी पाए जाते हैं।
